## GDP per capita (World Bank)

**1.** [Your answer: which indicator you chose and why. It must be in the same currency for all countries, adjusted for inflation, and go back as far as possible.]

**2.** [Your answer: the oldest year available.]

```{r}
# Search the World Bank indicators that match "gdp per capita"
wb_search <- WDIsearch("gdp per capita")
wb_search

# Import GDP per capita (constant 2015 US$) for all countries, up to 2025
# extra = TRUE adds region and income group (useful to drop aggregates later)
df_wb <- WDI(
  country = "all",
  indicator = "NY.GDP.PCAP.KD",
  start = 1960,
  end = 2025,
  extra = TRUE
)

# Oldest year with an actual value
min(df_wb$year[!is.na(df_wb$NY.GDP.PCAP.KD)])
```

# Part 2: Programming your own API functions

## Female labour force participation (ILO)

### Retrieve data using your own API wrapper

[Your 2-3 sentences: how the URL is built. Base URL + dataflow (agency, dataset ID, version) + key (one slot per dimension, separated by dots, empty slot = all values) + query parameters (start year, end year, format).]

```{r, file = "R/get_ilodata.R"}
```

### Test your API

**1.** [Your comment on the output of your own function.]

```{r}
# Countries to test (ISO 3-letter codes used by the ILO)
countries <- c("CHE", "USA", "DEU")

# Own function, applied to each country with lapply(), then stacked
df_own <- lapply(countries, get_ilodata, year_from = 2023, year_to = 2023) |>
  bind_rows()

# Keep the columns we need to compare
df_own_short <- df_own |>
  select(ref_area = REF_AREA, time = TIME_PERIOD, value_api = OBS_VALUE)

df_own_short
```

**2.** [Your answer: are the results the same as with Rilostat?]

```{r}
# Same request with the Rilostat package
df_pkg <- get_ilostat(
  id = "EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT_A",
  time_format = "num",
  filters = list(
    ref_area = countries,
    sex = "SEX_F",
    classif1 = "AGE_10YRBANDS_Y45-54",
    timefrom = 2023,
    timeto = 2023
  )
)

# Put both results side by side and compute the difference
comparison <- df_pkg |>
  select(ref_area, time, value_pkg = obs_value) |>
  inner_join(df_own_short, by = c("ref_area", "time")) |>
  mutate(difference = value_api - value_pkg)

comparison
```


## Bonus: GDP per capita (World Bank)

Optional.

### Import the data using your own API wrapper

```{r, file = "R/get_wbdata.R"}
```

### Test your API

[Your answer: are the results the same as with WDI?]

```{r}
# Own function, applied to each country with lapply(), then stacked
countries_wb <- c("CHE", "USA", "DEU")

df_wb_own <- lapply(
  countries_wb,
  function(cty) get_wbdata("NY.GDP.PCAP.KD", cty, 2023, 2023)
) |>
  bind_rows()

df_wb_own

# Same request with the WDI package
df_wb_pkg <- WDI(
  country = c("CH", "US", "DE"),
  indicator = "NY.GDP.PCAP.KD",
  start = 2023,
  end = 2023
)

# Put both results side by side and compute the difference
comparison_wb <- df_wb_pkg |>
  select(iso3c, year, value_pkg = NY.GDP.PCAP.KD) |>
  inner_join(
    df_wb_own |> select(iso3c, year, value_api = value),
    by = c("iso3c", "year")
  ) |>
  mutate(difference = value_api - value_pkg)

comparison_wb
```
